insight.headline: Taxes Recalculated
insight.what_changed: The orderUpdate GraphQL mutation now recalculates taxes when the shipping address is updated on an unfulfilled order. This change affects orders updated through the GraphQL Admin API. The new behavior ensures accurate tax calculations based on the updated shipping destination.
insight.developer_impact: Developers using the orderUpdate mutation should be aware of this change, as it may impact their app's tax calculation logic. They should review their code to ensure it handles the updated tax calculations correctly. Additionally, developers should test their apps to verify that the tax recalculations are accurate and consistent with the new behavior. The GraphQL Admin API will return the updated tax amounts in the order response, so developers should update their code to handle these changes.
insight.merchant_impact: Merchants will see accurate tax calculations on their orders, even when the shipping address is updated. This change ensures that merchants are charged the correct amount of tax, based on the updated shipping destination.
insight.why_it_matters: This change is important because it ensures accurate tax calculations and compliance with tax regulations. It also provides a better experience for merchants, who can rely on accurate tax amounts for their orders.

themes.title: GraphQL Admin API Enhancements
themes.detail: New fields have been added to cash management resources in the GraphQL Admin API, providing more detail about cash drawer balances and cash count activities. Furthermore, updating an order's shipping address now recalculates taxes as of August 31, 2026.

themes.detail: The shopify-account component is now a Theme Store requirement, and POS UI extensions can print directly to hardware receipt printers using the new Printing API. Shopify Functions API version 2026-10 has also added a createdAt field to the Customer object.
